summary.headline: Rathi Steel & Power Q1 FY27 total income rose 24.6% to INR193.67 crores, PAT up 84.5% to INR3.48 crores, with volumes up ~30% to 28,372 MT.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 showed strong volume growth, driven by TMT bars, which more than doubled to about 18,677 MT from about 8,200 MT a year earlier. Total income reached INR193.67 crores (+24.6% YoY), EBITDA INR7.77 crores (+24.83%), and PAT INR3.48 crores (+84.5%), taking PAT margin to 1.8% (+58 bps). Stainless steel volumes were soft, down roughly 10-12% YoY to about 9,000 MT, mainly due to export-linked end-users hit by freight costs and West Asia disruption. Management reiterated a rolling mill utilisation target above 60% for FY27 and a 20% revenue CAGR aspiration, while the TMT 550D direct-charging integration is still in trial and expected to ramp post-monsoon.

vs ~8,200 MT in Q1 FY26, more than doubled
Q1 and Q4 respectively; not disputed by management

segments.name: TMT bars
segments.commentary: Volumes more than doubled to ~18,677 MT; roughly 47-48% of revenue, sold ~100% in NCR, largely to real estate. Brand portion is only 48-50% integrated; 550D integration trial runs done, full ramp expected post-monsoon.

segments.name: Stainless steel
segments.commentary: Volumes ~9,000 MT, down 10-12% YoY on export-linked end-user weakness; roughly 52-53% of revenue. Management says it is more margin-accretive due to higher integration; 80-90% of range is 200 series.

guidance_outlook: Rolling mill utilisation expected above 60% in FY27 (FY26 was ~51-52%); management says it is on track.
Target of 20% revenue CAGR over the next two to three years, measured from FY25 base; management says achievable.
EBITDA margin improvement of 2-3 percentage points over about two years (FY27-FY28) cited as aspiration, from a range-bound 4-4.5%.
Expected FY27 capex of around INR15 crores plus, against INR4-5 crores spent so far, excluding new value-added projects.
Full-scale TMT 550D direct-charging ramp expected by Q4 FY27 after monsoon and pollution-related construction halts.
Melt shop expansion considered once utilisation exceeds 70-75%; refinancing with existing lenders being discussed to lower borrowing cost.
capex_capacity: Installed melting capacity ~85,000 tpa and rolling capacity ~2,00,000 tpa at Ghaziabad (~12.5 acres); rolling utilisation ~51-52% in FY26.
FY27 capex to date estimated at INR4-5 crores; full-year maintenance capex INR10-12 crores normally, with FY27 expected at INR15 crores-plus before debottlenecking/modernisation projects.
Direct-charging/melt-shop integration for TMT bars is in trial; teething issues being resolved across TMT sizes.
Rooftop solar still under feasibility assessment with suppliers; new sheds designed to accommodate it; no capex committed.
Renewable power ~20-25% of consumption via open access and exchanges, adjusted to price.
demand_pricing: Management expects softer steel realisations, volatile energy prices and geopolitical uncertainty to persist.
Stainless steel demand hit by export-oriented end-users due to high ocean freight and West Asia issues; management expects this to persist for a few months.
Competitive supply rose in stainless steel after several IBC acquisitions of similar units ~2 years ago; management says this is normalising.
Raw materials sourced ~100% domestically in Q1 to limit currency exposure; ferro alloys hedged against order book.
Credit period to customers ~30-40 days on average; order book held at about one month of orders.
Monsoon (Q2) and pollution-related construction halts (Q3) expected to dampen TMT demand; management cites the North-India and NCR construction pipeline as supportive.

qa_highlights.question: What monthly dispatch run rate in July-August, and is Q1 momentum sustaining?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not disclose monthly figures but hopes to maintain Q1 momentum; the equal split between construction and B2B segments helps offset monsoon weakness.

qa_highlights.question: Stainless steel volumes and Q2 trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Stainless volumes were ~9,000 MT, down 10-12% YoY, due to export-linked end-users hit by freight costs and West Asia disruption; management aims to recover to last year's level.

qa_highlights.question: Rolling mill utilisation and exit rate for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 utilisation was ~51-52%; management maintains guidance of above 60% for FY27 and says it is on track.

qa_highlights.question: Capex spent so far and full-year plan?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR4-5 crores spent in FY27 so far; around INR15 crores-plus expected for the year, mainly from internal accruals, excluding new projects.

qa_highlights.question: Margin levers and EBITDA target?
qa_highlights.answer: Levers are 20% growth, cheaper working-capital lines after refinancing, and 550D integration; management aspires to a 2-3 percentage-point EBITDA margin gain over about two years, with FY27 as an aspirational target.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital funding for the 30% volume increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Met mainly through extended supplier credit; management plans refinancing with existing lenders to get cheaper bank limits.

risks_watch: Stainless steel volumes down 10-12% YoY; recovery depends on West Asia freight and export demand.
Thin EBITDA margin (4-4.5% range-bound for three to four years, per analyst) despite volume growth; PAT margin only 1.8%.
Working capital dependence on supplier credit; bank limit enhancement contingent on refinancing at lower rates.
Monsoon (Q2) and NCR pollution-related construction halts (Q3) may slow TMT demand; full 550D ramp only expected by Q4.
Increasing stainless steel domestic supply from acquired IBC units.
Management did not disclose top-5/top-10 customer concentration or receivables outstanding; IR follow-up pending.
Revenue-based FY26 base (~INR700 crores per analyst) includes some past trading sales per management; 20% CAGR target needs sustained manufacturing volume growth.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volumes and the TMT ramp-up, but cautious on stainless steel and margins. Management was evasive on monthly run rates, customer concentration, receivables and the rooftop solar timeline, and gave no firm date for the solar decision.
key_quotes: We are not looking at turnover as a, or sales volume or sale price as our priority. We are looking at margins as the priority.

I may not have an exact number of the Q1 outstanding, but the credit period in the range of 30 days to 40 days maximum on an average.

growth.why: Management reiterates a 20% revenue CAGR aspiration (FY25 base) and >60% rolling mill utilisation in FY27 from ~51.5% in FY26, but the call gives no firm capacity, order or contract numbers behind them; the TMT 550D integration is still in trial with full ramp only post-monsoon, and stainless volumes fell 10-12% YoY.
